subject: Atlas demo: performance constraints, cost levers & pilot next steps
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@atlasretail.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Torres <marco@atlasretail.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo — Atlas perf goals and constraints

Thanks for the demo this morning, Sean — appreciate the focused walkthrough. Quick recap from our side and the must-haves we need to qualify for a pilot: 

- Latency: p95 single-turn generation <= 200 ms for short responses (<= 128 tokens). For long-form assistant sessions we need streaming with per-token latency under ~50 ms to keep a live typing feel.
- Concurrency: baseline 200 concurrent active sessions, with the ability to handle bursts up to ~1,000 concurrent users for promotions.
- Throughput: typical workload ~10k tokens/sec sustained across the fleet; bursts up to ~50k tokens/sec for short windows.
- Availability/SLAs: 99.9% during business hours; graceful degradation (fallback model) acceptable for rare overloads.
- Data: transient KV cache allowed; logs retained for 30 days. No long-term storage of PII.

Primary asks from Atlas to qualify: short quant estimate for the above targets, suggested configuration (hosted vs dedicated), and a 2–3 week pilot plan + procurement checklist.

I attached the sample prompts we used in the call and the recording. Can you send a rough cost/ops tradeoff matrix by EOD Wednesday?

Best,
Samira Khan
Director, Product
Atlas Retail

---
Attachments: sample-prompt-set.json (application/json), demo-recording.mp4 (video/mp4)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Marco Torres <marco@atlasretail.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo — Atlas perf goals and constraints

Samira — thanks for the clear list. Good news: everything you outlined is achievable, but there are trade-offs across cost, latency, and operational complexity. I've attached a concise SLO matrix (slo-matrix.xlsx) and put together two starter options to justify numbers quickly: 

Option A — Hosted, optimized runtime + caching (fastest time-to-pilot)
- Use Redwood hosted with continuous batching + prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts.
- Model: production-verified 8-bit quantized variant of the Llama-derivative we demoed.
- Expected p95 (short): 150–220 ms depending on burst profile; streaming per-token latency ~40–60 ms.
- Concurrency: scale horizontally; plausible baseline at 200 with autoscale; bursts up to ~1k with temporary warm-up and throttling policy.
- Pros: no infra on Atlas, faster setup, lower engineering lift.
- Cons: slightly higher per-token cost vs committed capacity at scale.

Option B — Dedicated capacity (reserved) + aggressive quantization
- Reserved GPU pool with optimized kernels, mixed quantization profiles (int4/int8 where acceptable).
- Model variants pinned for critical routes; local KV caching on dedicated nodes.
- Expected p95 (short): 110–180 ms; per-token streaming ~30–45 ms.
- Better unit economics at sustained >50k tokens/sec.
- Pros: predictable latency and cost at scale.
- Cons: procurement lag, setup time 2–4 weeks for reserved nodes.

Next steps I propose:
1) We (Redwood) deliver an itemized SLO/cost matrix by Wednesday (EOD).
2) Atlas shares a representative 24-hour workload + top 20 prompts (you already attached those — thanks).
3) Technical kick-off with Karthik and Ben for deeper sizing and preliminary pilot config.

I’ve looped Karthik for sizing/comments; Ben can comment on real-world batching and cache behaviors. If that plan sounds good I’ll also include a short pilot timeline and procurement checklist in the Wednesday deliverable.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Atlas demo — perf goals and constraints (internal ask)

Karthik/Ben — forwarding the Atlas recap. They need a quick, defensible sizing & tradeoff note for the two options I outlined. Can you please do the following by EOD Wednesday?

- Karthik: provide a rough mapping of latency p95 and per-token CPU/GPU cost for 3 quantization profiles (fp16, int8, int4) for the model family we demoed. Include realistic batch sizes (continuous batching) and KV cache hit assumptions (0%, 30%, 60%).
- Ben: call out expected streaming per-token latency ranges, warmup behavior under burst up to 1k conc, and operational controls (fallback model, throttles) we should propose.

Decision criteria Atlas cares about: latency bounds for short-turns, streaming responsiveness, concurrency headroom, and clear unit economics for pilot vs steady-state. Keep it concise (one page each).

Thanks — cc-ing Samira/Atlas for transparency.

Sean

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Atlas demo — perf goals and constraints (sizing note)

Sean — quick technical note (high-level bullets) to include in the SLO/cost matrix: 

- Quant profiles (short):
  - fp16: best quality; p95 short-turn ~90–140 ms on T4/A10 class kernels; batch sizes 8–16 for cost efficiency; unit token cost baseline.
  - int8: good quality/latency tradeoff; p95 short-turn ~120–180 ms; supports larger batch sizes (16–32) with reduced memory pressure; ~25–35% token cost savings vs fp16.
  - int4: aggressive; p95 short-turn ~140–220 ms depending on kernel; ~40–60% token cost savings; reduced quality on some prompt classes (we should flag top 5 prompts to validate).

- Continuous batching assumptions: 50–80 ms added latency for short-turns at batching windows tuned for 10–30 ms collection delay; net p95 depends on config (we can bias for lower latency at cost of throughput).

- KV/prefix caching: 30–60% effective token reduction on repeat-heavy flows (30% hit assumed for planning). Cache reduces bridging tokens but has low CPU cost; keep TTL short for PII protection.

- Streaming: per-token generation dominated by kernel throughput and small-token overhead; with our runtime and int8 we expect 30–55 ms per token end-to-end. Avoid quantization for critical small-turn routes where fidelity matters.

- Sizing: for Atlas baseline (~10k tokens/sec sustained) estimate 3–4 mid-tier GPUs in hosted mode with int8 + 30% cache hit; bursts to 50k tokens/sec need warm pools or autoscale to ~10–12 GPUs depending on model context length.

I’ll attach a one-sheet with rough numbers for the matrix. Ben — add streaming operational notes where you see fit.

Karthik
Applied ML — Inference Ops
Redwood Inference

Sean/Karthik/Ben — thanks for the quick turn. This looks sensible and aligns with our internal tradeoffs. Two quick asks before we sign off on a pilot: 

1) Pilot plan: please send a 2–3 week pilot plan that includes pilot acceptance criteria (p95 targets, max allowed error at int4 if used, streaming responsiveness), instrumentation hooks we require (per-route latency dashboards, token breakdown), and a rollback/fallback plan.
2) Procurement checklist: list of contract items and expected timelines for Dedicated vs Hosted pilot. Procurement is particularly interested in expected spend ranges for a 3-week pilot.

We’ll aim to confirm interest by end of week; procurement loop will need the checklist to scope internal approvals.

If you can include the pilot acceptance matrix and a small statement on data handling (KV TTL, log retention) in the same doc that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Director, Product
Atlas Retail
